title: Design and green synthesis of novel xanthine analogues as dual EGFR/CDK1 inhibitors: antiproliferative activity and  in silico  insights
content: A new series of 8-aryl-7-hydroxy-1,3-dimethylxanthines 4a–j were designed, synthesized and investigated as candidate dual inhibitors of EGFR and CDK1. Three methods (I–III) were used to synthesize the compounds starting from 6-amino-1,3-dimethyl-5-nitrosouracil (2) including an eco-friendly microwave-assisted method using ZnO nanoparticles (Method III). The 4f fluoro-substituted analogue was the most promising analogue, with the ability to inhibit EGFR (IC50 = 0.103 µM) and CDK1 (IC50 = 0.112 µM), compared with erlotinib (0.044 µM) and roscovitine (0.571 µM), respectively. When testing on an HT-29 cancer cell line, 4f exhibited moderate antiproliferative activity (IC50 = 39.44 ± 0.50 µM), which led to G0/G1 arrest, induction of apoptosis, and increased levels of Caspase-3 and Bax, whereas Bcl-2 levels, measured by ELISA, were at or near the assay blank and could not be reliably quantified. Molecular docking and normal-mode analysis (NMA) of 4f in the EGFR and CDK1 active sites suggested that 4f can be accommodated in both catalytic pockets, although its docking scores are weaker than those of the reference inhibitors. Despite the moderate cellular potency and limited selectivity over normal cells, these results suggest a starting point for further optimization of xanthine-based inhibitors toward dual EGFR/CDK1 inhibition.
